answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to hold a time-locked stake in a shared vault: the stake acts like a ledge an agent stands on, and proven fraud shoves it off, burning the deposit. New agents start with tiny limits and earn larger ones only through attested work, so copying one trusted identity into thousands of cheap fakes is unaffordable. Reputation then grows like a sonnet, line by line, earned slowly and lost in a single verse.
